5. No smoke or fog machines inside the tower. Exterior fog machine allowed only if wind is
   below 10 mph and directed away from the tower.
6. No paint, chalk, or adhesive on any surface. Use gaffer tape only on the floor, and remove
   at the end of each day.
7. The caretaker's residence (north side of the property) is off-limits except for emergency
   access. No parking in front of the residence.
8. Vehicles over 3 tons must stay on the paved lot. Do not drive on the bluff trail.
9. Waste: all trash must be packed out. No dumpster on site. Portable toilets are at the lower
   meadow, serviced daily.
10. Fire ban in effect (per Forest Service order). No open flame, no smoking outside the
    designated area (paved lot, south corner).

Addendum A (Exterior grounds):
- The lower meadow may be used for base camp tents only. No stakes deeper than 6 inches.
- The bluff trail may be closed to the public for up to 30 minutes at a time, but only with
  two posted signs and a PA at each end. No full-day closure.

Addendum B (Interior):
- Maximum 8 people in the tower at any time. This includes cast, camera, and sound.
- The lantern room is a confined space. No more than 3 people in the lantern room at once.
- No furniture, props, or equipment may be placed on the stair treads. Handrail must remain
  clear at all times.
- The original 1888 Fresnel lens is in place. Do not touch, move, or clean the lens. No
  lighting units within 3 feet of the lens.

Cannon Beach Soundstage is a converted warehouse at 1420 S. Hemlock St., Cannon Beach, OR 97110. The facility is used for interior builds that require controlled light and sound: the keeper's quarters re-dress, the lantern room close-ups, and the basement storage scenes (12A, 12B, 13C). The stage is not a listed historic structure, but it sits within the Cannon Beach downtown overlay zone; exterior signage changes and any generator use between 22:00 and 07:00 require prior written approval from the city. The building has one loading dock (east side), two production offices (north end), and a green room with a kitchenette. There is no dedicated parking for crew; use the municipal lot at 2nd St. and Hemlock, two blocks south. The lot fills by 08:30, so carpool or arrive early.
